issues.description: In the solution, the Book struct declares the title property as `private let title: String` (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift:26). However, Client.main() accesses `book.title` from a different file (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift:11). Declaring the property `private` prevents access from Client (private limits visibility to the enclosing declaration/file), which causes a compile error and contradicts the intended use of the Book’s title for output. The problem statement describes a Book with a title and author (problem_statement.md:16-18) and the exercise expects the client code to read the title when printing the inventory. This visibility restriction is an unintentional structural inconsistency that will block students or confuse them when following the example/solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Book.title property accessible to Client. Remove the `private` modifier (use `let title: String`) or use a broader access level (e.g., internal/public) so that code in Client.swift can read `book.title`. This preserves the intended design (title as a let constant) while allowing the client to print the inventory.
